title: China strikes Guam and the Pacific bases: the first hour (simulation)

strikes.launch_name: PLA Rocket Force DF-26 brigade, Zhejiang (location simulated)
strikes.notes: Conventional follow-on at Kadena (A15, A20 saturation logic, assumption).

strikes.launch_name: PLA Rocket Force brigade, Fujian (location simulated)
strikes.notes: Conventional, as in 002 and the CNAS game (A25). DF-17 nuclear role is unsubstantiated (002 D).

strikes.launch_name: PLA Rocket Force DF-26 brigade, Shandong (location simulated)
strikes.notes: Conventional on the home port of the only forward-deployed US carrier (002 A26, A18). Simulated assumption.

strikes.launch_name: PLA Rocket Force DF-26 brigade, southern China (location simulated)
strikes.notes: SIMULATION choice: the one nuclear shot, 10 kt, the top of the Pentagon's 'below 10 kiloton' low-yield estimate (A10) on a DF-26 nuclear-capable delivery (A5, A6); about half of Nagasaki's yield. Hero strike.

strikes.launch_name: PLA Rocket Force DF-26 brigade, Zhejiang-Jiangxi border (location simulated)
strikes.notes: Conventional, Naval Base Guam about 48 km from Andersen (A14). Simulated assumption.

strikes.launch_name: PLA Rocket Force DF-26 brigade, central China (location simulated)
strikes.notes: Conventional, most DF-26s have conventional missions (A6); CNAS/Pettyjohn games open on Guam (A25).

strikes.launch_name: H-6K bomber over East China Sea (location simulated)
strikes.notes: H-6K with CJ-20 land-attack cruise missiles (A9); launched earlier to arrive with the ballistic wave. Subsonic timing from engine.

model: Glasstone and Dolan scaling calibrated to NUKEMAP Hiroshima figures; flight times fitted to published ranges; all values are estimates for a labelled simulation.
